A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CIE research. The complete main text, Appendices A–H, equations, tables, and figures are readable and can be matched across pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original response-length experiments across three language models, comparisons with prompting and RULER, and generation-quality evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a training-data scaling experiment comparing CIE with RULER.

M1.justification: Both versions learn two endpoint embeddings, interpolate a control embedding, and append it to instruction embeddings during fine-tuning and generation. v2 explains placeholder replacement and decoding more explicitly but does not establish a changed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Both use VERBOSITYCTRL train/val/range, Alpaca-LI, and the RULER-style length evaluation. The new experiment varies training-data fractions within existing coverage; it introduces no dataset, task, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: The prompting and RULER comparisons are retained, including the appendix's three prompts, Random, and Best baselines. The added scaling experiment reuses RULER without changing comparator membership in the existing experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 adds LLaMA-3-8B experiments training CIE and RULER with 25%, 50%, and 75% of the training data alongside the existing 100% setting, reporting PM/FM. The previously documented metrics, model configurations, preprocessing, and training and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 2 adds a training-data sensitivity analysis asking whether CIE's advantage over RULER persists across data fractions. This is a limited extension using one model; the previous prompt-sensitivity, response-length distribution, and generation-quality analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the new scaling table introduces none. Existing dataset statistics and box-and-whisker reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 adds reduced-data results: at 25%, CIE achieves PM/FM of 13.08/16.32 versus RULER's 11.80/14.20, with additional results at 50% and 75%. Its 100% entries repeat v1's results. The matched original benchmark tables, appendix tables, and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The control-matrix definition, interpolation equation, and bounding procedure are unchanged. v2's discussion of embedding geometry and conditioning is explanatory prose, without new formal assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions present interpolated embeddings as the central contribution and claim more reliable response-length control than prompting and discrete control while preserving generation quality. The new supporting experiment and revised future-work examples do not materially change those core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds persistent-bias and ordinal-geometry explanations for CIE, linking them to generalization with fewer examples and contrasting them with RULER's token-growth requirements. The conclusion redirects future-work examples toward sentence/character counts, complexity, toxicity, and bias. The existing Limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: Section 2 newly specifies a control placeholder without vocabulary expansion, replacement of its positions with interpolated embeddings before transformer processing, and standard autoregressive generation. These are additional implementation disclosures. Appendix processing, hyperparameters, hardware, and inference details remain unchanged; the code/data link is relocated.

R1.justification: The cited works and Related Works section are retained. Section 4 nevertheless expands positioning against RULER by explicitly arguing that continuous embeddings encode ordinal relationships and avoid the need for additional length-specific tokens when extending word-count control.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized edits to the abstract and introduction, expands the method explanation, rewrites the conclusion's future-work paragraph, and adjusts correspondence and acknowledgment text. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the scaling table, renumbers the existing tables, revises Figure 1's caption, moves Figure 2 between columns, and places the existing Figure 3 on a separate appendix page. The original graphics and table structures are retained within the same two-column format.

improvement.justification: The new scaling experiment provides useful evidence that CIE's advantage persists with reduced training data, and Section 2 makes implementation clearer. These are limited gains: the experiment covers one model without run-to-run uncertainty, and it does not isolate the geometric or attention mechanisms asserted in the added explanations. The original evidence is preserved.
